chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Ja'far ibn Bashir from Yunus from Minhal al-Qassab said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'I make a mistake in the prayer while I am behind the Imam.' He said, 'When he (the Imam) gives the salam, perform two prostrations and do not rush.'

key_terms.أَسْهُو: I make a mistake / I am forgetful

ai.seo_question: What should one do if they make a mistake in prayer while following the Imam?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the specific protocol for a follower who commits an error during congregational prayer, mandating that the corrective prostrations (sajdatay al-sahw) be performed individually after the Imam's final salam rather than in unison. The instruction 'wa la tahabb' (do not rush) emphasizes the solemnity and deliberation required in rectifying the prayer, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the distinct legal status of the follower's prayer relative to the Imam's. This ruling highlights the practical jurisprudence of the Ahl al-Bayt regarding the nuances of congregational worship and the individual responsibility of the worshipper to ensure the validity of their own act of devotion.
